name: NVIDIA Blackwell datasheet (GB200 NVL72 / GB200 NVL4 / HGX B200) - every Tensor Core row printed sparse-only, retrieved and re-read row by row
publisher: NVIDIA-authored document, served from reseller CDN nor-tech.com (document footer '4204213. Oct 25' per the first-party copy already recorded as vb-nvidia-blackwell-datasheet-firstparty)
notes:
VERBATIM 2026-10-04, retrieved with curl and parsed with pymupdf. HOST CAVEAT, WHICH IS THE REASON THIS RECORD EXISTS ALONGSIDE THE FIRST-PARTY ONE: the existing source vb-nvidia-blackwell-datasheet-firstparty already carries NVIDIA's OWN hosted copy of this document at dam-cdn.nvd.orangelogic.com, so this record is deliberately NOT presented as better evidence. Its purpose is narrower - it is the row-by-row re-read of the HGX B200 column against the dense/sparse footnotes, because the B200 record's column attribution was previously wrong (see the discrepancy list) and re-reading the reseller copy is how the error was found. The spec text of the reseller copy and the first-party copy was compared on the Technical Specifications table and is IDENTICAL, including the 'PLFOPS'-style typos, which is itself evidence they are the same document.

FOOTNOTES, VERBATIM:
footnote 1: 'Specifications in sparse | dense.'
footnote 2: 'Specifications in sparse. Dense is one-half of the sparse spec shown.'

WHICH CONVENTION APPLIES TO WHICH ROW: on this sheet EVERY Tensor Core row carries footnote 2 - the sparse-only, halving convention - including 'FP4 Tensor Core2' and the 'Total NVFP4 Tensor Core2' system row. This is the crucial difference from the Blackwell ULTRA sheet, where the FP4 row instead carries footnote 1, the labelled Sparse|Dense pair. The two sheets are near-identical in layout and differ precisely on the row the repo is most likely to get wrong.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE HGX B200 COLUMN, DENSE AS PUBLISHED: FP4 18 PFLOPS -> 9 PFLOPS dense = 9,000 TFLOPS; FP8/FP6 9 -> 4.5 PFLOPS dense = 4,500 TFLOPS; FP16/BF16 4.5 -> 2.25 PFLOPS dense = 2,250 TFLOPS; TF32 2.2 -> 1.1 PFLOPS dense = 1,100 TFLOPS. FP32 75 TFLOPS and FP64 37 TFLOPS carry no marker and are dense as printed.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE GB200 NVL72 COLUMN, DENSE AS PUBLISHED: FP4 20 -> 10 PFLOPS; FP8/FP6 10 -> 5 PFLOPS; FP16/BF16 5 -> 2.5 PFLOPS; TF32 2.5 -> 1.25 PFLOPS; FP32 80 and FP64 40 unmarked and dense.
SELF-CONSISTENCY CHECK THAT SETTLES THE COLUMN QUESTION: 8 GPUs x 18 PFLOPS sparse = 144 PFLOPS, which is exactly the 'Total NVFP4 Tensor Core2 144 PFLOPS' printed in the HGX B200 column of the same table; and 8 x 9 PFLOPS dense = 72 PFLOPS, matching the second figure of that same pair '144 | 72 PFLOPS'. The GB200 NVL72 pair '1,440 | 720 PFLOPS' is 72 x 20 and 72 x 10. So the GB200 system row is ALSO a sparse|dense pair here, printed under footnote 2, with the pair already expanded. A reader who takes '144 PFLOPS' as dense gets a figure 2x the dense per-GPU number on the same sheet.
